strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Runtime-controlled task.run provider failures now return and record bounded structured failure outcomes instead of requiring JSON-RPC error string parsing.
The existing task-run network and sensitive prompt guards remain enforced while their failures become classified next-action outcomes.
LlmRequestFailed and SecondPassLlmRequestFailed events carry bounded failure class, retryability, next action, and fingerprint metadata.
Headless callers can branch on deterministic provider failure fields and replay the same terminal outcome without duplicate TaskRunning.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances llm_provider_execution with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: task.run returns bounded llm_provider_failure outcome metadata for controlled provider failures including configuration, network guard, HTTP, invalid response, missing content, and transport classes.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Existing strict provider failures returned JSON-RPC internal errors and ledger reason previews, forcing headless callers to parse human strings.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Autonomous provider recovery cannot reliably choose whether to fix configuration, authorize network, inspect provider health, redact prompt context, or retry later.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M11.3 added headless continuation budgets and M12.1/M12.2 added external Mode Pack policy boundaries; M13.1 changes LLM provider execution failure behavior.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. Existing task.run and run.events behavior is extended without adding a method.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. This adds bounded execution-result metadata, not a report, digest, history, readiness, preview, or status wrapper.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Controlled provider failures mark the task Failed and return TaskRunResult.llm_provider_failure instead of a JSON-RPC internal error; replay returns the same bounded outcome without duplicate TaskRunning.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Controllers can branch on failure_class, retryable, next_action, request_phase, and failure_fingerprint.
answers.milestone_progress: M13 gains its first runtime-owned provider execution failure boundary, enabling later explicit retry or recovery admission work.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M13.1 changes the deterministic current phase manifest. Review must confirm task.run provider failure behavior, replay safety, and bounded evidence rather than a wrapper or guard-only phase.

exit_criteria: Strict missing provider configuration returns TaskRunResult.status Failed with llm_provider_failure.failure_class configuration_missing
Missing BROWNIE_LLM_ALLOW_TASK_RUN_NETWORK returns network_not_authorized without contacting the provider
Mock non-2xx provider response returns http_status with bounded status metadata
Mock missing choices or missing message content returns missing_provider_content
Replaying task.run for the same failed task returns the same structured failure fingerprint without duplicate TaskRunning
Existing successful fake and mock provider task runs remain compatible and do not include llm_provider_failure

Ledger and RPC evidence excludes raw prompts, raw provider responses, raw request bodies, file content, stdout, stderr, commands, environment values, API keys, secrets, absolute paths, and canonical paths
No new RPC, diagnostics wrapper, readiness report, digest, history, status wrapper, preview, automatic retry, or VSIX-owned provider policy path is added
next_phase_candidate_notes: M13.2 may add bounded explicit provider-failure retry admission keyed by failure_fingerprint, without automatic retry or guard bypass.
next_phase_after_m13_1: M13.2 Explicit LLM Provider Failure Retry Admission
